findings.element: h2.trayName / span.tag (src/tasks.css:773-778, 1101-1106) · h2.b-measureHead / p.b-todayLabel / h2.b-behindLabel / h1.b-who (src/timeline.css:67-68, 506-513, 536-544) · b "Filing under" / span "Your notes" / span.peelLabel / span.darkTag (src/notes.css:108, 397, 647, 967, 1370, 1430)
findings.problem: The uppercase micro-label — the object that says 'this names a region', and the most repeated typographic unit in the suite — renders at five specs, split cleanly along the old product borders. Measured at 1920 across eight states: Tasks is Geist Mono 11px/400, +0.10em, leading 14px; Timeline is Geist Mono 11px/400, +0.16em, leading 15.4px (plus 12px/400 +0.20em on h1.b-who); Notes is Geist 11px/600, +0.075em, leading 15.95px, and 12px/600 +0.075em on .darkTag. So walking the spine from TO DO to DAYS AWAY changes the label's letterfit by 60% (1.1px vs 1.76px of tracking at the same 11px), and walking to FILING UNDER changes its family and its weight as well. Three separate declarations exist for one role: --tr-cap: 0.075em (notes.css:108), a hard 0.1em literal (tasks.css:777 and :1104), --track-label: 0.16em (timeline.css:67). The audit gate already reports this and does not pass it: 'Geist Mono|11|label → 1.1px vs 1.76px  h2.trayName "To do" | span "one of three"'. The suite's own claim is one application; the label tier is the place a reader can see the seam.
findings.fix: Declare the tier once, at :root in src/shell.css beside --t-11, as three roles at one size rather than three products at one role: --label-face: var(--font-mono); --label-size: 11px; --label-weight: 400; --label-lead: 15.4px; --track-label: 0.14em (region label: trayName, b-measureHead, b-behindLabel, Filing under, Your notes, peelLabel, specName); --track-label-tight: 0.10em (inline datum label: span.tag, darkTag); --track-label-wide: 0.20em (ceremonial top line: h1.b-who only). Then point all three products at them: replace the 0.1em literals at tasks.css:777 and :1104 with var(--track-label) and var(--track-label-tight); set notes.css:108 --tr-cap: var(--track-label) and change the six uppercase Notes rules (397, 647, 1236, 1370, 1430, and 967 to --track-label-tight) from font-weight 600 to var(--label-weight) with font-family var(--label-face); alias timeline.css:67 --track-label to the shell token and keep --track-labelWide pointing at --track-label-wide. Leave the .railAvatar / .dockAvatar initials on Geist 600 — a monogram is not a label — and give them their own --track-monogram: 0.075em so they stop borrowing --tr-cap.

findings.element: span.word inside header.tlHead — src/across.css:398-406 (line-height: var(--lead-body)) and src/timeline.css:94, :160 (--lead-body: 1.5, --stage-pad: 40px); compare src/tasks.css:2447 (line-height: 22px) and :257 (padding: 0 28px), src/notes.css:256 (line-height: var(--lh-tight))
findings.problem: Round 5 flagged this and it was not changed, so here is the measurement, taken at 1920 with all three sheets starting at exactly (100, 18). The wordmark's FIRST BASELINE sits 36.00px below the sheet's top edge in Tasks and 36.13px below it in Notes — a 0.13px agreement, which is a real contract, not a coincidence. In Timeline it sits 58.00px below: the same 17px/600 word, 22px lower. Horizontally Tasks puts it 28px in from the sheet's leading edge (tasks.css:257 states that 28px IS the sheet's one leading edge, shared with the view pill, the tray label and every card) and Timeline puts it 40px in (--stage-pad). The mechanical cause of part of the drop is a leading error: the wordmark takes line-height: var(--lead-body), and --lead-body is declared at timeline.css:94 as '1.5 · all prose, 13 to 20px' — a prose leading on a wordmark, giving 25.5px against Tasks' declared 22px and Notes' 21.76px. Three leadings on one object. This matters more in a suite than it did in three standalone products: the wordmark is the ONE element whose entire job is to hold still while the word inside it changes, so that switching the spine reads as a change of label rather than a re-layout. Driving the spine Tasks → Timeline, the identity jumps 22px down and 12px right, and it is the only thing on the head that moves.
findings.fix: Two lines. In src/across.css:401 replace `line-height: var(--lead-body)` with `line-height: 22px` (matching tasks.css:2447, and inside the 11-27px ramp the wordmark already sits on). Then bring the head's leading edge and first baseline onto the suite's: in src/across.css:393-397 change `padding: var(--stage-pad) var(--stage-pad) 0` to `padding: 19px 28px 0` — 19px top puts the 22px-leading wordmark's baseline at 36px below the sheet edge, matching Tasks and Notes to within a pixel, and 28px is the stated leading edge. Keep --stage-pad for the measure and the blocks below the head, which are a different object; only the head's own padding changes. Re-check the @media (max-width: 430px) override at across.css:423, which should become `padding: 19px var(--gap-line) 0` so the phone head keeps the same first baseline.

findings.element: p.trayNote — src/tasks.css:782 ([data-app="tasks"] .trayNote { min-height: 1.4em; }); the caption carries no text-wrap at all, unlike .cardTitle (:921 balance) and .cardNote (:936 pretty)
findings.problem: The lane caption is the only text block in Tasks with no widow control — computed text-wrap is `wrap`, greedy — and its reserve is one line (min-height: 1.4em = 16.8px). tasks.css:907 names this exact omission as 'the real objection' when arguing the cardTitle rule, and then leaves it in place on the caption. Measured at 1920 and 1440, on the shipped board: the collapsed WAITING lane is 172px wide against the others' 372px, so its 43-character caption wraps to two lines and rags to a three-word runt, 'or a decision.' Its caption bottom is 200px against 183px for the other four, and its first content item sits at y=227 against y=197 — the five lane heads stand on two baselines and the head row of the board is visibly ragged in the delivered 1920 frame. It gets worse in the 1100-1179 band, which no gate width covers: at 1100, REVIEW's caption also goes to two lines and WAITING's to three, so the first cards stand at 298 (To do, In progress, Done), 314 (Review) and lower still (Waiting) — three baselines on five lanes at the last width where the board is still a board. The collapse of an empty lane is a designed decision; its typographic consequence was not.
findings.fix: Two declarations at src/tasks.css:782. Replace `[data-app="tasks"] .trayNote { min-height: 1.4em; }` with `[data-app="tasks"] .trayNote { min-height: calc(1.4em * 2); text-wrap: balance; }`. `balance` is the correct law for a caption of two or three lines and it is already the file's choice for every other short block (.cardTitle :921, .drawerRow > span :1685, :2266, :2656); it removes the 'or a decision.' runt by evening the two lines. The two-line reserve puts every lane's first card on one baseline at every width from 1100 up, which is the property the board's head row is asserting and currently does not hold. Costs 17px of head height on the four one-line lanes, which is the price of the shared baseline; if that is unacceptable, the alternative is `min-height: calc(1.4em * 2)` scoped to `.board:not(.listBoard) .trayNote` only, so the list view keeps its tighter head.

findings.element: h1.headName — src/tasks.css:287-292 (20px/600, --tr-19, ink-1) vs src/notes.css:287 (var(--t-15)/400, --tr-14, color: var(--ink-2)); the competing objects are span.word (17px/600, src/shell.css:535) and button.headNext b (15px/600, src/notes.css:285)
findings.problem: tasks.css:288-291 writes the suite's rule down in the file: 'The sheet's own title is the largest thing on it. Four sizes inside a 2px band, all at 600, gave the top of the scale no rank at all.' Measured in the 60-66px head band at 1920, one product of three keeps it. Tasks: h1 'The Orchard, events' at 20px/600 in ink-1 is the largest text on the sheet head, 3px above the wordmark — clean, one title, one rank. Notes: the same class on the same element is 15px/400 in ink-2, so the h1 'All your notes' is the THIRD-ranked object in its own head, out-ranked by span.word 'notes' at 17px/600 and tied on size but beaten on weight by the sibling button.headNext b 'Mara & Finn' at 15px/600. The largest word on the Notes sheet head is the product's own name; the largest word on the Tasks sheet head is the venue. Timeline puts its h1 (h1.b-who 'Mara & Finn') at 12px/400 Geist Mono uppercase — the smallest text in the product. So a person walking the spine gets three different answers to 'which word on this head tells me where I am', and in Notes the answer is a 15px grey label sitting between two darker, heavier neighbours, with a 100px gap and no size step to separate the h1 from the toggle beside it. That is the one thing a shared head has to get right, and the rule to get it right is already written in the repo.
findings.fix: In Notes, put the rank on the object that actually names the sheet. Move the h1 from 'All your notes' onto the filing name (the b inside button.headNext at src/notes.css:285) and set that rule to `font-size: var(--t-20); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: var(--tr-21); color: var(--ink-1); line-height: var(--lh-title);` — 20px/600/ink-1, matching tasks.css:292 exactly. Then demote src/notes.css:287 .headName to the scope-label tier it actually is: `font-size: var(--t-13); font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: var(--tr-13); color: var(--ink-3);` and drop its h1 tag to a span, so 'All your notes' reads as the breadcrumb it is rather than a heading nobody can find. Leave Timeline's 12px mono ceremonial line where it is — the 148px '79' is that sheet's title and Direction B is the founder's — but give timeline's sheet head the 20px/600 title slot too by promoting the .b-switch timeline name (src/timeline.css, 15px/600) to var(--size-lead)+3 / 600 / --track-head, so all three heads step 20 → 17 → 13 from title to wordmark to metadata.
